name: DCM Atlantic 1972: Hold the Gap
description:
15 July 1972. Ten days ago, an hour before dawn, the guns opened up along the whole length of the Iron Curtain. By nightfall Soviet tanks were across the Elbe; within the week they stood on the North Sea, with Jutland and the Danish islands behind them. Paratroops came down on Norway's airfields one after another, from the North Cape to Stavanger, and only Oslo still holds. In the south the Black Sea Fleet followed the tanks through Thrace and out past Istanbul, and Cairo and Damascus have thrown open their harbours to the Soviet squadron.

The Navy paid first. The carriers that were at sea when it began are gone, caught in the opening days by missiles from submarines and bombers no one saw coming. Forrestal lived only because she was in the yard: she lies at Norfolk now with her air wing aboard, the last flat-top NATO has in the Atlantic. At Naples the cruiser Little Rock gathers what is left of the Sixth Fleet, and the German, Danish and Norwegian crews who fought their way out wait at Den Helder and Oslo for orders.

Those orders are yours. The Northern Fleet is coming out through the gap between Greenland, Iceland and Britain, with a landing force for Iceland in its wake; another is gathering in the Black Sea off the northern mouth of the Bosporus, waiting for its chance at Crete. Soviet submarines are spread across every lane from Norfolk, and without the convoys Britain and the Mediterranean will run out of fuel and weapons within weeks.

Hold the gap. Bring the convoys through. Then take back what was lost: Norway, Denmark, Germany's ports, the Straits, and the Soviet harbours in Egypt and Syria. The war is won when our flag flies over every base beyond the Warsaw Pact's own soil, and lost if theirs flies over everything we hold outside North America and the Western European mainland, Oslo excepted.

texts.guideWar: July 1972. The Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact struck first: Norway but Oslo, northern West Germany to the Rhine, Denmark and the Turkish Straits have fallen, and the front reaches into the Netherlands and Belgium. Egypt and Syria have opened their ports to the Soviet fleet. You command NATO at sea: the US Second and Sixth Fleets and the allied navies, from Canada and Norway to Italy, Greece and Turkey.
texts.guideWarTask: Two landing forces are at sea: the Northern Fleet's for Reykjavík (Keflavik falls with it) and the Black Sea Fleet's for Souda Bay in Crete. Stop them, keep the convoys from Norfolk coming, then take back what was lost.
texts.guideExampleMove: The Western Approaches Escort holds south of Ireland. Right-click west of the Hebrides: it plots a route round the coast and shows its arrival time at each waypoint.
texts.guideExampleSplit: Split the frigates off CVBG Forrestal to escort a convoy to the Clyde, then merge them back when it is safely in.
texts.guideLift: Battalions ride in landing ships: Austin 2 · Charleston or Newport 1 · Fearless 2 · Sir Lancelot 1 (the enemy's Alligators 2).
texts.guideLiftIslands: Select the group and right-click an enemy port: every airfield here falls with its port.
texts.guideExampleInvade: Phibron 4 at Norfolk carries 7 battalions (Nashville and Trenton 2 each; Charleston, Newport and Manitowoc 1 each). Tromsø, a minor port, is held by a garrison of 2, Alexandria, a naval base, by 3: bring gun escorts, whose fire adds up to 50 %.
texts.guideExampleCarrier: Forrestal loses 6 F-4Js and 2 A-7Es over the Norwegian Sea. Her open places fill only with aircraft flown aboard: order F-4Js and A-7Es at a field in her reach, then REBASE them to her, or give a flight Land at… her. Her magazine refills at a naval base with aviation stores, Norfolk or Faslane; at Reykjavík, a port, it can't.
texts.guideReplen: Sacramento (fuel and weapons), the T2 oiler (fuel) and Kilauea (weapons) are in the Shipyard panel, under Replenishment (their card says what each carries). In a friendly port they load from its stock, never taking it below half of what it should hold.
texts.guideTanker: You have no tanker aircraft in this campaign: the game has no land-based tanker of 1972 (no KC-135 or Victor), and Forrestal's KA-3Bs aren't campaign tankers. How a tanker works:
texts.guideExampleStrike: Forrestal's A-6Es with a Strike loadout on Bodø Air Station from the Norwegian Sea (MISSION: Strike a base, from her AIR OPS) before your landing in Norway: fewer Su-24s to meet your landing ships.
texts.guideExampleSupply: Souda Bay is about to be fought for: set it to High so its missiles are topped up before the landing comes.
texts.guideExampleIntel: "SOSUS reports surface ships 140 nm from Tórshavn, position approximate": the red circle on the map is that area, not a firm position.
texts.guideCarrierPrices: Their price in the Shipyard panel. Carriers by tier: Forrestal 1,250, Enterprise 1,400. Yours cost 10 % less and join with all their helicopters and 30 % of each fixed-wing type.
texts.guideVictory: The first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil wins: for you, everything outside the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact countries, islands, Egypt and Syria included (Norway, Jutland and the Danish islands, West Germany's ports, the Straits, Alexandria, Tartus...); for the enemy, everything outside North America, the Western European mainland (Oslo excepted) and Greenland.
texts.guideRoad: Stop the landings on Iceland and Crete, get the convoys through, then take back Norway (Tromsø brings Langnes with it), Jutland, West Germany's ports, the Danish islands and Bornholm, the Straits, and last the Soviet squadron's ports in Egypt and Syria (Alexandria, a naval base, is held by 3 battalions).
texts.guideReplenStart: Service Squadron 2 at Norfolk, the Sixth Fleet's group at Naples, the RFA tankers at Faslane and HMCS Provider at Halifax start loaded.
texts.guideBatteries: (NATO: M110 guns; Norway: coastal guns; Soviet: Redut coast-defence missiles and 2S3 guns; East Germany, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Egypt and Syria: BM-21 rockets)
texts.guideSams: (NATO: Nike Hercules; Britain: Rapier; Portugal, Canada and France: M42 guns; Iceland: as the US; Soviet: SA-2, SA-3; East Germany, Egypt: SA-3; Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Syria: SA-2)
texts.guideEnemy: It starts with 182 ships: the Northern Fleet's cruisers in the Norwegian Sea, submarines across the convoy lanes, the Baltic Fleet west of Bornholm, the Black Sea Fleet north of the Bosporus and the 5th Eskadra east of Crete. After its landings on Reykjavík and Souda Bay, its landings come one at a time: for Lerwick, Karljohansvern, Salamis, Izmir and Limassol.
texts.guideSamReach: Nike Hercules 70 nm, SA-2 25, SA-3 15, Rapier 4
texts.endingWon: The last base the enemy held beyond its own soil has fallen. The Northern Fleet is back behind the North Cape, the Straits are open again, and the convoys sail to Europe unmolested. The war is won.
texts.endingLost: The enemy holds every base we had beyond North America and the continent. The gap is open, the convoys have stopped, and what is left of the fleet has fallen back to its last harbours. The war is lost.
texts.procurementLift: a place in an assault ship (Austin 2 · Charleston or Newport 1 · the enemy's Alligators 2)
texts.messageVictory: Victory. Every base beyond {enemy}'s home soil is ours: the campaign is won.
texts.messageDefeat: Defeat. {winner} holds every base we had beyond North America and the continent: the campaign is lost.
texts.sitrepNote: The clock is paused: Space starts it
texts.sitrepNoteTip: Press Space, or Play in the time controls (top right), to start the clock. New to the campaign? The Guide (the book at the bottom of the left strip) starts with your first hour.

situation: The Soviet Union and its Warsaw Pact allies opened hostilities without warning ten days ago. Norway from the North Cape to Stavanger, northern West Germany up to the Rhine, Jutland, the Danish islands with Copenhagen and Bornholm, and Thrace with the Turkish Straits have been overrun, and the Soviets have pushed into the Netherlands and Belgium; in Norway only Oslo holds out, in Germany the Rhineland and the south. Egypt and Syria have joined them and opened Alexandria and Tartus to the Soviet Mediterranean squadron.

The Atlantic carriers were lost at sea in the first days. Forrestal is the only carrier left, at Norfolk with her air wing aboard. In the Mediterranean the Sixth Fleet has no carrier; Little Rock's cruiser group lies at Naples.

The allies hold what is left: the Royal Navy at Faslane, the Canadians at Halifax, the Norwegians at Oslo, the West German and Danish ships that escaped with the Dutch at Den Helder, the French at Brest and Toulon, the Italians, Greeks and Turks in the Mediterranean.
Everything Britain and the Mediterranean need now comes by sea from Norfolk.
enemy: The enemy is on a war footing. The Northern Fleet's missile cruisers are believed at sea in the Norwegian Sea, its submarines in the Norwegian Sea, north of the Iceland-Faroes gap, and across the convoy lanes from America; Bear-D reconnaissance aircraft are shadowing our groups.

A Northern Fleet landing force is at sea in the Norwegian Sea; Iceland is feared to be its object. A Black Sea Fleet landing force is gathering in the Black Sea off the northern mouth of the Bosporus with Moskva and Leningrad, and a landing on Crete is feared once it is through the Straits.
The Soviet 5th Eskadra is believed east of Crete with submarines in the Ionian Sea and west of the Sicilian Narrows. Egyptian and Syrian fast attack craft and fighters operate under its cover.
Further landings are expected against the Faroes, Shetland, Oslo, Britain, the Mediterranean islands, Greece and Turkey's coasts.
intent: Hold the gap. Iceland is not to be given up while there is a ship to fight for it.
Hold Crete. The Sixth Fleet and the Hellenic Navy are to meet the landing before it is off Souda Bay.
Keep the sea lanes open. Without the fuel and weapons from Norfolk neither Britain nor the Sixth Fleet can fight.
Preserve Forrestal, rebuild the fleet, then take back what was lost.

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Istanbul
firstOrder.briefing: With Thrace and the Straits in Soviet hands, everything the Black Sea Fleet sends to Istanbul, and on through the Straits to its ships in the Aegean, sails from Sevastopol across the open water to the west of you. Yours is the only allied boat inside the Black Sea. Work that traffic and sink the tonnage this order asks for on the lanes into Istanbul within 5 days.

firstOrder.title: Watch the Kola Inlet
firstOrder.briefing: Every Northern Fleet ship bound for the gap, and every tanker and transport sent after it, must come out of the Kola Inlet past Severomorsk. Its escorts and maritime patrol aircraft are close at hand, so keep deep and keep moving. Keep your boat within 40 nm of the marked point off the inlet for 18 hours in all within 2 days, and report what sails.

firstOrder.title: Stop the Iceland landing force
firstOrder.briefing: The Northern Fleet's landing force for Iceland is reported far to the north of you, off the island's north-east corner, with its missile cruisers closed up round it and Echo-class boats out ahead of it. It is steering for Reykjavík, and if its troops get ashore there, Iceland and the gap go with it. Go north and meet it before it rounds the island: find the landing group and sink at least one of its ships within 3 days.

firstOrder.title: Guard Souda Bay
firstOrder.briefing: The landing force out of the Black Sea is gathering off the Bosphorus with its helicopter cruisers and will come south through the Straits and the Aegean, and Souda Bay is believed its object; the 5th Eskadra's missile group is reported to the east of you. Souda is the Sixth Fleet's only harbour on Crete. Close the island and keep a ship within 60 nm of Souda Bay for 12 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Clear the northern approaches
firstOrder.briefing: Soviet submarines are reported to the north of you, working the approaches to the North Channel close to the lane from Norfolk to Faslane. Every convoy for the Clyde has to pass them. Find them and sink at least one boat within 4 days.

starts.name: Southern North Sea, east of England

firstOrder.title: Cover the Den Helder lanes
firstOrder.briefing: Den Helder is the last allied port on the continent's North Sea coast, and its lanes, in from Norfolk by the Dover Strait and out to Rosyth, the Shetlands and Oslo, all cross these waters within reach of the Soviet-held German Bight. Put your group on the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) on the nearest stretch of them and keep it on station for 18 hours in all within 3 days.

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Kaliningrad
firstOrder.briefing: The Baltic Fleet's base at Kaliningrad draws its supplies from Leningrad, by a lane that runs down the length of the Baltic to its door. The water is shallow, its warships and bombers are close, and there is no allied port this side of the Skagerrak. Get onto that lane and sink the tonnage shown on this order within 4 days; whatever of its traffic you meet in battle counts as well.

firstOrder.title: Strike the Bornholm cruiser group
firstOrder.briefing: A Soviet cruiser group is reported west of Bornholm, off Rügen, covering the crossings to the Danish islands and the landing ships at Kaliningrad. It is the only enemy group at sea within your aircraft's reach, a long flight over Soviet-held Denmark. Find it and sink at least one of its ships within 3 days.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Malta lane
firstOrder.briefing: Malta lives on the lane from Naples: Valletta and its airfields draw everything that way. Soviet submarines are reported to the west of you, beyond the Sicilian Narrows. Take your group onto the lane under the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) and stay on station for 12 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Hold the Dover Strait
firstOrder.briefing: With the German Bight in Soviet hands, the Dover Strait is the gate the enemy must force to reach the Channel, and the lane from Norfolk to Den Helder runs through it. Take your group up the Channel and keep a ship within 25 nm of the strait for 12 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Screen Toulon
firstOrder.briefing: The Escadre de la Méditerranée lies at Toulon, France's only naval base in the Mediterranean, and the Soviet submarines reported west of the Sicilian Narrows may be working north towards the Provence coast. Keep a ship within 30 nm of Toulon for 18 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Strike the Crete landing force
firstOrder.briefing: The Black Sea Fleet's landing force is reported gathering off the northern mouth of the Bosphorus, with Moskva and Leningrad in close company and submarines ahead of it. It will come down through the Straits and the length of the Aegean, and Crete is believed its object. The Hellenic Navy is to meet it among the islands before it is off Souda Bay. Go north, find it as it comes out of the Dardanelles, go for the landing ships themselves and sink at least one ship of that group within 4 days.

firstOrder.title: Hunt the boats bound for Chios
firstOrder.briefing: Black Sea Fleet submarines have left the Bosphorus ahead of the landing force and its helicopter cruisers. They are expected between Chios and Skyros within a day or so, to hold the way to Crete open and to close the approaches to İzmir. Do not wait for them here: go north to meet them as they come out of the Dardanelles, hunt them down the Aegean and sink a boat within 4 days.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Sinop lane
firstOrder.briefing: Sinop is the last allied port on the Black Sea, and its only lane comes in along the Anatolian coast from the Bosporus, within reach of the Black Sea Fleet's bombers at Saki. Keep the nearest stretch of it covered by patrol aircraft on the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) for 18 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Close the Denmark Strait
firstOrder.briefing: With the Iceland-Faroes gap fought over, Soviet submarines and raiders may take the long way round Iceland, through the Denmark Strait, to the convoy lanes and the western approaches to Reykjavík. Keep a ship within 30 nm of the marked point in the strait for 24 hours in all within 2 days, and report anything that comes through.

starts.name: North Sea, between Scotland and Norway

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Haakonsvern
firstOrder.briefing: The Soviets hold Haakonsvern, and everything their garrison at Bergen needs comes round from the Baltic by the coastal lane past Lista and Stavanger, east of you. Every cargo that fails to arrive brings the day we take Bergen back nearer: sink the tonnage this order calls for on the lanes into Haakonsvern within 4 days.

firstOrder.title: Strike the Baltic cruisers off Bornholm
firstOrder.briefing: The Baltic Fleet's cruiser group lies west of Bornholm, off Rügen, covering the crossings, and Oslo expects a landing from the Baltic as soon as it has an escort. It sits at the edge of your strike aircraft's radius: hit it there and put at least one of its ships on the bottom within 3 days, before it can come north.

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Wilhelmshaven
firstOrder.briefing: Wilhelmshaven and the Jade are in Soviet hands, and their supplies come the long way, out of the Baltic, round the Skaw and down the Jutland coast past you. Until we take Germany's ports back, starve them: this order gives the tonnage to sink on the lanes into Wilhelmshaven within 5 days, and the traffic met in battle there counts too.

firstOrder.title: Defend Den Helder
firstOrder.briefing: Den Helder holds the Dutch fleet and the German and Danish ships that fought their way out, and no other allied port is left on this coast, with the Soviet-held German Bight just to the east. Keep a ship within 25 nm of Den Helder for 24 hours in all within 2 days.

firstOrder.title: Hunt the boats in the Ionian
firstOrder.briefing: Missile and diesel submarines of the 5th Eskadra are reported in the southern Ionian Sea, well to the south of you, working north towards the lanes from Naples to Greece and Crete. Taranto's ships and the Sixth Fleet's convoys will have to pass them. Take your group down the Ionian to meet them before they are across the lanes, find the boats and sink at least one within 4 days.
